title: Copilot Studio: block sharing of agents that embed maker credentials
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap record and Microsoft documentation. The documented controls, default, publishing exceptions and licensing caveats are accurately represented; existing sharing and runtime access are correctly distinguished from later sharing and publishing enforcement.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Copilot Studio evaluates agent connections and can prevent sharing or publishing when they violate connection-sharing policy.
claims.quote: When you enforce this setting, Copilot Studio evaluates the connections used by an agent and can prevent the agent from being shared or published when a connection violates the organization's connection-sharing policy.

claims.claim: Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials is an environment-level Power Platform admin center control for Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: The Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials setting is an environment-level control for Microsoft Copilot Studio agents.

claims.claim: Unsafe sharing requires at least one connection that does not allow credential sharing.
claims.quote: An agent is considered unsafe for sharing when both of the following conditions are true: ... The agent uses at least one connection that doesn’t allow credential sharing.

claims.claim: The unsafe connection also uses design-time credentials instead of individual user authentication.
claims.quote: The connection uses credentials supplied at design time instead of asking each user to authenticate with their own credentials.

claims.claim: As dependency-based enforcement becomes available, an unsafe called flow or agent can make its calling agent unsafe.
claims.quote: As dependency-based enforcement becomes available, an unsafe dependency can cause the calling agent to be treated as unsafe for sharing.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: Connections using end-user credentials are not subject to this connection-sharing restriction.
claims.quote: Connections configured to use end-user credentials aren't subject to this connection-sharing restriction because each user authenticates by using their own connection at runtime.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: All sharing allowed detects and informs makers of unsafe credential use without blocking sharing.
claims.quote: All sharing allowed | Copilot Studio detects and informs makers about unsafe credential use, but doesn’t block sharing.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Safe sharing enforced blocks applicable publishing and sharing paths for unsafe agents.
claims.quote: Safe sharing enforced | Copilot Studio blocks applicable publish or share paths when an agent is unsafe for sharing.

claims.claim: Makers can still edit and save unsafe agents under enforcement.
claims.quote: When Safe sharing enforced is selected, makers can still edit and save an unsafe agent, but they can't newly share it.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Enforcement prevents newly sharing a violating agent with viewers or end users.
claims.quote: You can't share an agent that violates a connection-sharing security policy with a user who has viewer or end-user access.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Enforcement prevents sharing a violating agent with everyone in the organization for end-user access.
claims.quote: Similarly, you can't share the agent with everyone in your organization for end-user access.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Channels that distribute an agent on publication without a separate Share action can have publishing disabled for maker user credentials.
claims.quote: Some channels make an agent available as part of publishing and don’t provide a separate Share action. ... If the agent uses the maker’s user credentials at runtime, Copilot Studio marks the agent as unsafe and disables publishing while enforcement is active.

claims.claim: An authenticated agent that has not been shared can publish successfully.
claims.quote: For authenticated agents, an agent that you didn't share can publish successfully

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: An already-shared authenticated agent that violates the policy is blocked from later publishing when enforcement applies.
claims.quote: an agent you already shared with another user is blocked from publishing when enforcement applies.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Approved service principals, API keys or managed identities can permit publication when the connection supports the scenario.
claims.quote: Agents that use an approved system identity, such as a service principal, API key, or managed identity, can be published when the associated connection supports the scenario.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Enforcement does not retroactively unshare or disable previously shared agents.
claims.quote: Enabling enforcement doesn’t retroactively unshare or disable agents that were previously shared.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Scope
claims.claim: This control governs sharing and publishing, not runtime blocking.
claims.quote: The sharing agents with embedded maker credentials control governs sharing and publishing. It doesn’t block an agent while the agent is running.

claims.claim: Configuring safe sharing requires permission to manage settings for the target environment.
claims.quote: To configure Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials, you need permission to manage settings for the target Power Platform environment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The settings reference requires System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions to update environment feature settings.
claims.quote: Make sure you have the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions to update the settings.

claims.claim: Affected tools are marked Blocked with a Sharing policy violation message.
claims.quote: These tools are marked as Blocked with a Sharing policy violation message explaining that a connection violates the administrator's connection-sharing policy.

claims.claim: A tool also restricted by a data policy shows Data policy violation instead.
claims.quote: If a tool is also restricted by a data policy, Copilot Studio surfaces the Data policy violation message instead.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; What's changing: publishing exceptions
claims.claim: The Publish option becomes unavailable for the publishing blocks described in the briefing.
claims.quote: When Copilot Studio detects a blocking condition before publishing, the Publish option is unavailable and makers are directed to review the agent's status.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The security route configures individual environments or environment groups using the documented Don't let makers and Let makers credential-sharing options.
claims.quote: You can configure the setting for an individual environment or an environment group. ... Don't let makers share agents with their own credentials embedded (recommended) ... Let makers share agents with their own credentials embedded

claims.claim: The documented environment route is Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features > Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.
claims.quote: Go to Manage > Environments, and then select the environment that you want to configure. ... Select Settings, and then select Features. ... Find Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The group route is Power Platform admin center > Security > Threat detection > Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials > Environment groups > environment group > Set up.
claims.quote: select Security, and then select Threat detection. ... Select Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials. ... In the Environment groups tab, select the environment group for which you want to configure the setting. ... Select Set up.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The existing sharing-limits route is Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Edit Managed Environments > Manage sharing.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environments. ... select a managed environment. ... In the command bar, Edit Managed Environments. ... The sharing rules are located in the Manage sharing section.

claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $governanceConfiguration saves modified sharing-limit configuration.
claims.quote: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $governanceConfiguration

claims.quote:

claims.claim: The agent security-group and viewer-limit properties are bot-limitSharingMode and bot-maxLimitUserSharing under settings.extendedSettings.
claims.quote: -Name 'bot-limitSharingMode' -Value "ExcludeSharingToSecurityGroups" -Force ... -Name 'bot-maxLimitUserSharing' -Value "20" -Force

claims.claim: The editor-sharing property is bot-authoringSharingDisabled under settings.extendedSettings.
claims.quote: $governanceConfiguration.settings.extendedSettings | Add-Member -MemberType NoteProperty -Name 'bot-authoringSharingDisabled' -Value True -Force

claims.claim: The existing Managed Environments sharing limits govern editors, viewers, security groups and viewer counts rather than evaluating embedded credentials.
claims.quote: Use the Editor and Viewer roles to control sharing ... Only share with individuals (no security groups) ... Limit number of viewers who can access each agent ... Control sharing of agents that use maker-provided credentials
